text:
maria: Quick intake — runtime QoS prioritization for Dedicated customers. Problem: we keep getting customer requests to guarantee tail latency under load for mixed-priority traffic (high-priority inference vs background batch). Current runtime has best-effort batching and a single autoscale pool per tenant. We need a scoped PRD to propose options and acceptance criteria.

maria: Goals: 1) define minimum viable prioritization (e.g., preemptive slot reservation or fast-path lanes), 2) surface obvious perf/cost tradeoffs, 3) specify rollout criteria for Dedicated.

maria: Non-goals: full per-request costing model, reworking serving runtime from scratch, adding new model shapes. Keep changes targeted to request routing/pool controls and simple runtime knobs.

maria: Success metrics (proposal): p50/p95/p99 tail latency for HP traffic under 2x, 5x baseline load; throughput degradation for LP traffic <= 20% at target; cost increase <= 15% for most customers.

sam: +1. Can we get a sketch of concrete options? do we mean request priority tagging + queue sharding, or separate reserved GPU slices?

jess: Sketch: option A: tagging + priority-aware scheduler (soft priority, no hard preemption). Option B: reserved slots (hard capacity reservation for HP requests). Option C: fast-path micro-VMs for HP (higher cost/perf iso). Each has different rollback and infra complexity.

eli: Edge cases to call out: waterfall requests where a single HP call fans out many internal LP calls; multi-tenant interference if we reserve too much; cold-start impact for reserved slots. Also need fallback policy if reserved pool saturates — should we spill to best-effort or throttle?

maria: Acceptance criteria proposal (short):
```
- Deployable to Dedicated with feature flag.
- HP requests meet p95 latency target in 2/3 synthetic load tests and 90% of customer real workloads in canary.
- Observability: per-priority SLO dashboards + alert when spillover > 5%.
- Rollout: canary (1 tenant), gradual ramp (10, 50, 100), auto-rollback on regressions.
```

sam: For tests, we need clear load profiles. I'll attach synthetic profiles tomorrow. One question: do we allow customers to opt in to reserved slots (pay more) or enable by default?

maria: Prefer opt-in for Dedicated as a paid addon. Default would be best-effort with recommended knobs from Optimize.

jess: Implementation notes: minimal path: add priority header in API, runtime uses separate request queues per priority, dequeue policy favors HP with admission control; reserved slots requires capacity accounting + billing changes.

eli: Ops: add tracing to show when HP spilled over, and a dashboard showing cost delta per-tenant. Also add a short runbook for support: how to explain tradeoffs and rollback steps.

pm-bot: FYI — created JIRA ticket INF-1829 with summary "Runtime QoS: prioritization options & rollout plan". Assignee: @maria.

maria: Thanks — next steps: Sam to post synthetic profiles, Jess to draft rough rollout timeline + infra complexity estimate, Eli to draft observability/runbook bullets. I'll synthesize into a short PRD by EOD Friday. Tagging @jess @eli @sam for comments. :thumbsup:
